thread:
Sam (AE): Quick sync — Acme POC kickoff. Need final prompt inventory + baseline prompts, plus success criteria. Can we lock these today?
Maya (Solutions): Yup. I pulled their initial use cases: ticket triage -> categorization, automated reply drafts, and search re-ranker.
Lee (ML Eng): For the POC we'll need ~5 canonical prompts per use case, 10 negative examples, and 50 eval pairs for quality checks.
Sam (AE): Timeline check: customer expects 3-week POC. Week 1 = prompt collection + sandbox, Week 2 = iter + evals, Week 3 = perf tuning + handoff. Agree?
Arjun (Customer): Confirmed 3 weeks works. We can provide raw sample tickets and 200 anonymized chat snippets by EOD tomorrow.
Maya (Solutions): Great. Two asks for Arjun: 1) a sensitivity tag per file (PII / low / none), 2) the top-3 business rules to preserve in replies.
Arjun (Customer): We'll add sensitivity tags. Top rules: never promise timelines, always include next-steps, always escalate if required.
Lee (ML Eng): Baseline prompts — sharing starter templates below. We'll iterate them during week 1.
```
Prompt: "You are an assistant that drafts internal support replies. Given the ticket, produce a concise reply (2-3 sentences) that includes next steps and whether escalation is required. If sensitive info is present, redact specifics and note type."
Example instruction tokens: temperature=0.0, max_tokens=150, top_p=1.0
```
Maya (Solutions): Suggest we create a prompt inventory CSV with columns: prompt_id, use_case, intent, example_input, expected_output, eval_metric. Can sales ops create the skeleton?
Sales Ops: On it — I'll push a Google Sheet and invite Arjun.
Lee (ML Eng): Success criteria proposal (suggested):
- Quality: >80% pass on 50 eval pairs (binary accept/reject by SME)
- Hallucination: <3% critical errors
- Latency: median < 300ms for generate call with our hosted model (or note if using dedicated)
- Throughput: handle 20 rps steady during peak tests
- Security: all customer data flagged as PII sanitized in results
Elaine (Security): We'll need to run the customer security questionnaire and confirm network requirements. Arjun, do you want Private deployment for the POC or hosted with encrypted transport?
Arjun (Customer): Hosted is fine for POC if we can sign an NDA and ensure data is encrypted at rest. Private would be preferred long-term.
Sam (AE): Pricing question from procurement: do we bill POC as usage-only or offer a short-term credit/discount? Sales Ops, advise.
Sales Ops: Recommend a usage-based bill with up to 25% credit for POC hours if they convert to Dedicated within 60 days. I'll draft the quote.
Maya (Solutions): Action items: 1) Sales Ops create prompt inventory sheet (today) 2) Arjun provide samples + sensitivity tags (tomorrow) 3) Lee and I prepare baseline prompts and eval harness (end of day) 4) Elaine start security Qs (tomorrow)
Sam (AE): Perfect. If anyone hits blockers on the prompts or needs extra eval pairs, ping me. :thumbsup:
Arjun (Customer): Thanks all — will upload samples tonight.
Elaine (Security): Uploaded the initial security checklist link: https://redwood.internal/sec/acme-poc-checklist (internal)
Lee (ML Eng): One more note — include a short prompt variant for "low verbosity" and "concise" modes; helps measure length-vs-quality tradeoffs.
Maya (Solutions): I'll add those variants to the inventory template.
Sam (AE): Cool, closing loop — we'll reconvene after prompt inventory is shared.
Deploy Bot: New doc created: /sheets/acme-poc-prompt-inventory (Sales Ops)
